headline: Highest risk is medium: both research agents can browse, call external APIs, and share broad networked workflows, creating plausible prompt-injection, leakage, and output-cascade paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents can run browsers and use networked research workflows, so attacker-controlled web content can plausibly enter one agent and be passed to the other through files or outputs. gpt-researcher explicitly uses MCP and file I/O, while RD-Agent consumes research artifacts and logs; no provenance guard is documented. The interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced, so uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF either agent ingests web content or generated files from the other without provenance checks, prompt injection is possible.
IF a shared workspace or manual copy-paste bridge is used, attacker instructions can traverse the pair.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of untrusted HTML/Markdown into downstream prompts.
Add a provenance header and strip instructions from retrieved content.
Review browser-sourced text before passing it between agents.
Use separate workspaces for each agent.
requires-engineering: enforce content-type allowlists at the orchestrator boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch research documents and send data to third-party model APIs by default, so sensitive local documents, reports, or logs can leak if routed through the pair. gpt-researcher handles local documents and broad API egress; RD-Agent writes logs and calls multiple external APIs. No shared filesystem is documented, but the default networked workflow makes leakage plausible.
conditions: IF either agent processes confidential documents or logs, those contents may be transmitted to external inference APIs.
IF the two agents share a workspace or exchange files, sensitive material can propagate across both outputs.
mitigations: Keep confidential data out of both agents' inputs.
Separate credentials and API keys per agent.
Turn off file ingestion for sensitive runs.
Review logs for secrets before sharing artifacts.
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before any API call.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances and broad networked research, so they can contend over shared mutable resources if pointed at the same workspace, APIs, or datasets. gpt-researcher can read files and spawn subprocesses; RD-Agent writes logs and uses external APIs. No locking or isolation between them is documented, so overlapping writes are plausible.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write into the same directory, file clobbering or stale reads can occur.
IF both agents mutate the same external resource or dataset without locks, race conditions can corrupt outputs.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Serialize writes to shared resources.
Run one agent at a time for mutable tasks.
Use per-agent API credentials and quotas.
requires-engineering: add file and resource locking in the orchestrator.

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher is a content-writing/research agent that can generate citations and reports, and RD-Agent is a research agent that can consume those artifacts. If RD-Agent treats gpt-researcher output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream research traces or logs. The pair lacks documented verification gates, so the safer medium severity is warranted.
conditions: IF RD-Agent consumes gpt-researcher reports without independent verification, hallucinations can propagate.
IF either agent auto-renders the other's citations or facts into final artifacts, downstream errors become persistent.
mitigations: Require a human review step between agents.
Cross-check claims against original sources.
Mark inter-agent outputs as untrusted by default.
Limit automatic reuse of citations.
requires-engineering: add verification scoring before downstream action.

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents handle research data and logs, but their profiles show different data classes and cloud/API ecosystems, which can create retention or residency mismatches when the same dataset is processed by both. gpt-researcher handles local documents and multiple external APIs; RD-Agent stores logs and uses Azure/OpenAI/Kaggle services. No explicit residency or retention alignment is documented, so mismatch risk is medium.
conditions: IF EU personal data or regulated research data is routed through both agents, residency and retention obligations may diverge.
IF one agent's logs retain data longer than the other's workspace, deletion requests may be incomplete.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in both agents.
Document retention settings for each service.
Separate datasets by jurisdiction.
Review vendor terms for each API.
requires-engineering: implement retention and deletion controls across both pipelines.
